summary: In 1930-1932 Union Carbide and contractor Rinehart & Dennis drove the Hawks Nest Tunnel through near-pure silica in West Virginia without wet drilling or respirators, killing hundreds of mostly Black migrant workers from silicosis and burying many in unmarked graves.

evidence.note: story set at Gauley Bridge, Fayette County, West Virginia, in 1930
Union Carbide subsidiary hires Rinehart & Dennis, contract shifts liability to the contractor
first earth turned on the tunnel on 31 March 1930
mostly Black migrant workforce, segregated shacks and scrip pay
dry drilling, no respirators for Black workers, crews forced into dust after blasts
company doctors misdiagnose silicosis and hand out placebo pills
undertaker paid per body dumps Black workers in a mass grave
lawsuits from 1932, state trials 1933-1934, mines director changes testimony
1936 House inquiry condemns the companies and a respirator law follows
segment on Muriel Rukeyser's investigation trip and FBI surveillance
NPR Frontline 2018 findings on today's silicosis epidemic among miners

notes: Covered span starts at the 1930 dig; Union Carbide's 1911-1919 origins and dam get only a few minutes of setup and the ancient history of silicosis is background. End is 1938, publication of Rukeyser's Book of the Dead (general knowledge), quoted throughout. Modern miner silicosis and Union Carbide's later fate set reaches_present. medical-malpractice is light (company doctors, a few minutes). Union Carbide could arguably be co-primary.
